findings.title: PR body claims deferrals are recorded in deferred-work.md, but no gauge entries exist
findings.detail: The two known-limitation pins (loop->feed_drop_sites call-site pin; SLA text draw-path pixel pin) live only in PR prose. deferred-work.md holds only the two pre-existing entries (3.2 lane QoS, routing-bandwidth-cost) — the durable deferral register was never updated.
findings.recommended_fix: Append the two gauge-telegraph deferrals to deferred-work.md (source_spec/summary/evidence, matching the existing entry shape).

findings.title: SLA eased display numbers lack a draw-path mutation leg — bypassing gauge_read in draw_sla_gauges fails no test
findings.detail: The briefing's mutation standard holds for the health/pool bars (palcheck section 6, independently re-verified this round) but not the SLA readouts: deleting either gauge_read call keeps unit, wiring, golden, and palcheck gates green — the strobe silently returns on the text surfaces.
findings.recommended_fix: Move the eased-readout formatting into app/render (harness-importable) and palcheck it, or pin the display-number derivation from an app-package test; the deferral is acknowledged in the PR body but undurable (see the deferred-work finding).

findings.title: Terminal gauge snap (the r1 game-over-freeze fix) ships unpinned — deleting it passes every gate
findings.detail: The gauge_reset call lives inline in main's fixed-timestep loop, unreachable by the pullback-style wiring tests. Deleting it returns the frozen mid-ease lose-screen fill with every gate green.
findings.recommended_fix: Extract the terminal transition (mode set + gauge_reset) into a seam proc like start_run/feed_drop_sites and pin it with the pullback_test_app fixture: arm a mid-ease state, drive the proc, expect gauges unseeded.

findings.title: PR body verification counts are stale vs the shipped tree (91/46 claimed; 94/48 actual)
findings.detail: The r1 fold appended its section but never refreshed the numbers: gauge_test.odin adds 11 tests (83+11=94) and gauge_wiring_test.odin adds 2 (46+2=48). Independently re-measured this round: 94 render / 48 app / 261 core, all green. The counts contradict the PR's own r1-fold commit message.
findings.recommended_fix: Update the verification line to 94 (83 + 11) / 48 (46 + 2) or annotate the counts as pre-r1-fold.

findings.title: PR body ships both 'Roster cap 8' and 'SLA slots 8 -> 16' for the same SLA ease slots
findings.detail: The Decisions bullet states cap 8 as shipped while the same body's r1 section and the code ship 16 slots ([16]Gauge_Ease). One of the two statements is false; reviewers reading the bullet will mis-review the code.
findings.recommended_fix: Rewrite the Decisions bullet to the 16-slot roster headroom, deleting the stale cap-8 rationale.

findings.title: Advisory test gate: CONCERNS
findings.detail: P0 (golden byte-identity / unfed contract) 100% — unit + draw-level + goldens (49 demos re-run green this round). P1 ~80%: terminal snap, SLA draw seam, pool ghost leg unpinned. Overall ~83%.
findings.recommended_fix: Raise P1 to >=90%: extract+pin the terminal transition, add the SLA eased-readout draw-path leg, add the pool-ghost palcheck leg; durably record the two deferrals.

findings.title: gauge_test.odin comments still describe the superseded 8-slot SLA table (slots are 16)
findings.detail: Header says 'roster > 8 unfed' and the roster-cap comment says 'the 8-slot table' while the assertion two lines below pins len(v.gauges.sla_ms) == 16.
findings.recommended_fix: Update both comments to 16 (or drop the number: 'roster beyond the slot table').

findings.title: Chunk-ghost draw block duplicated across the two bar gauges
findings.detail: Identical ghost geometry/alpha math in two files; a future cue-craft change must be made twice and can silently diverge — the same drift risk pool_fill_pct/sla_avg_ms were extracted to kill.
findings.recommended_fix: Extract a shared draw_chunk_ghost(v, g, raw_pct, col, bar_x, bar_y, bar_w, bar_h) helper called from both bars.

findings.title: gauge_wiring_test.odin imports render via ../app/render; every sibling uses ./render
findings.detail: Functionally identical, but inconsistent with the app package's uniform import convention (main, pullback_test, noc_toggle_test, qos_panel_test, settings_test all use ./render).
findings.recommended_fix: Change to `import rnd "./render"` to match the siblings.

findings.title: Pool-bar chunk-ghost draw block unpinned — health twin has palcheck 6(c), pool has none
findings.detail: Deleting the pool ghost block fails no test: gauge_flash_read is unit-tested generically and palcheck 6(e) never renders a chunk state. One of the two flash cues is mutation-survivable at the draw level.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a 6(e) chunk leg mirroring 6(c): seed 100, chunk to 20, render at age 1 — scan the ghost band blends over the track, then pure track after expiry.

findings.title: CHUNK_SLA_MS per-unit threshold wiring never exercised by any test
findings.detail: No test anywhere references CHUNK_SLA_MS (0 hits outside gauge.odin): swapping it to CHUNK_PCT in gauge_tick, or reintroducing the unit confusion the r1 round fixed, fails nothing.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a gauge_tick test: seed sla_ms at 10ms, jump avg to >=35ms, assert the tween re-anchored while sla_loss stays on its pct threshold.

findings.title: Loop->feed_drop_sites call site unpinned (pre-existing debug_surface_smoke class)
findings.detail: The wiring test drives the seam proc directly; deleting the loop's call disables the entire gauge feed (and drop marks) with every gate green — the engagement call needs a headless app-drive harness (same class as debug_surface_smoke).
findings.recommended_fix: Land the headless app-drive harness story that can pin the loop call site; record the deferral durably (see the deferred-work finding).

findings.title: pool_fill_pct boundary clamps (packets > cap, cap <= 0) untested
findings.detail: The shared derivation owns the off-frame guard but all existing coverage is sub-cap (cap 200/2 packets; cap 100/55) — a future refactor of the clamp or the degenerate-cap guard fails nothing.
findings.recommended_fix: Extend the feed test: 150 packets / cap 100 -> target exactly 100; cap 0 -> no divide-by-zero, pct bounded.
